title: The bidri alloy
description: A label card of the bidri alloy with the zinc, copper and silver shares the Hyderabad quality-marking scheme set. Place it where the alloy is introduced.

u0002.text: Bidriware is cast from a zinc-copper alloy, engraved and inlaid with silver.

C001.text: Bidriware is a metal craft of Bidar in which designs engraved on a cast zinc-copper alloy are inlaid with silver.

quotes.quote: Bidri ware is a famous handicraft of Bidar District.
Bidriware is an alloy ofzinc , copper and other non ferrous metals. Pretty designs are engtaved on it and there after inlaid with pure silver ware.
The technique consists of casting objects from a high-zinc alloy and then inlaying them with silver or brass, or a combination of both.

C089.text: The census monograph reproduces quality-marking standards set for Bidriware at Hyderabad, requiring a base alloy of 93% to 94% zinc and 6% to 7% copper and inlay silver of at least 96%.

quotes.quote: a quality marking scheme was introduced in the State first on a voluntary basis in 1960
The scheme was extended by phases to the other crafts also, including Bidriware at Hyderabad.
Those set up for Bidriware are reproduced below: 1. Base alloy should have the following com position: Zinc = 93% to 94% Copper = 6% to 7%
Silver used for inlay work shOUld contain a minimum of 96% silver
